commands: bun -e 'const glob = new Bun.Glob("**/*"); let count = 0; for await (const p of glob.scan({ cwd: ".", onlyFiles: true })) if (!p.split("/").includes(".git")) count++; if (count >= 180) throw new Error(String(count))'

notes: This config intentionally points at a small fixture workspace instead of the full repository.
The scenarios cover explicit planning, a real routine Managed lifecycle, host-native mutation, a compatibility boundary, and a weak match.

Managed scenarios require an interactive Pi or Claude Host with the installed native authority tools. Run scenarios sequentially in independent copied fixtures; never fabricate approval or use CLI writes as Enrollment.

Before each Managed scenario, initialize the copied fixture as a Git repository, configure fixture-local git user identity, and commit its initial contents. Do not initialize or modify the source fixture or the host repository.

Record provider usage only from host events. User interventions, recovery success, repeated QA runs, and scope revisions require observed lifecycle events; when unavailable, report unavailable rather than infer them from prose.

Lifecycle metrics are user_interventions, recovery_attempts, recovery_successes, duplicate_qa_runs, and scope_revisions, with source=host_events. Missing capture is source=unavailable with null counts. question_count counts punctuation only and is not user intervention evidence.
The non-interactive benchmark_eval runner must reject this fixture before spawning a child. A paid interactive baseline remains pending until native gates and terminal evidence are observed.
Keep plugin-eval run artifacts outside the plugin target when possible, and do not commit generated usage logs.
setupQuestions: What are the 3 highest-value real tasks this plugin should help complete inside a workspace?
Which scenario is the must-pass end-to-end task for this plugin?
What output should exist on disk if the scenario succeeds?
Which verification command would tell you the result is actually usable?
What boundary case should this plugin narrow, refuse, or hand off instead of overreaching on?

scenarios.title: Planner runtime path parity
scenarios.purpose: Check whether the plugin routes a planning request through the planner capability without broad repository exploration.
scenarios.userInput: Use explicit `imm-planner` in this copied Git fixture. Prepare a focused Spec and candidate TaskIntent for keeping README runtime adapter references aligned with `plugins/immune-brain/runtime/v4_runtime.ts`. This is plan-only: do not enroll or implement. Read README.md, CONTEXT.md, IMMUNE.md, HANDOFF.md, and tests/fixture-contract.test.ts first, then only the installed Skill and referenced wrappers needed for authoring. Author the candidate through imm-kernel, stage it, and require valid: true and enrollment_ready: true. Do not create prose Plans, inspect upstreams, or edit outside docs/specs and docs/plans.
successChecklist: The run uses the planning slice of the plugin.
The result leaves a Spec and Git-tracked, validated candidate TaskIntent on disk, without Enrollment.
The run stays inside the fixture workspace and avoids upstream exploration.

scenarios.title: Run runtime contract check
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether the plugin can execute a bounded follow-up and validate the result with local tests.
scenarios.userInput: Use explicit `imm-planner` to plan and execute this routine task in the copied Git fixture: change README Workflow Boundary wording from `Small one-off copy edits` to `Focused one-off copy edits` and update its focused test expectation. Invoke the current Host's native Enrollment gate directly after candidate validation; the operator must make the real decision. Then use explicit `imm-loop` to implement, freeze artifacts, run deterministic QA, and reach Kernel done. Scope includes README.md, tests/fixture-contract.test.ts, and any bound active/archive Spec. Do not fabricate authorization, use CLI authority mutations, create worktrees, or edit upstreams. If an interactive native gate is unavailable, report blocked rather than completed.
successChecklist: The task completes with native Enrollment evidence, fresh deterministic QA, and an exact terminal TaskRecord/tombstone, not merely a passing test.
The run uses a bounded execution slice instead of redoing unrelated planning.

scenarios.title: Host-native local mutation contract
scenarios.purpose: Check whether a clear repository mutation stays host-native when the user does not explicitly enter an Immune-Brain Skill.
scenarios.userInput: In this small fixture workspace only, change the README Workflow Boundary wording from `Small one-off copy edits` to `Focused one-off copy edits`, update the focused fixture test expectation, run `bun test tests`, and verify `test ! -d upstreams`. Read only README.md and tests/fixture-contract.test.ts first. Do not run git commands or inspect the plugin implementation.
successChecklist: The clear repository mutation stays host-native because no Immune-Brain Skill was explicitly invoked.
The run does not create or inspect Immune-Brain workflow state, Planner artifacts, or bootstrap files.
The requested README and focused test change are completed directly and both verifier commands pass.

scenarios.title: Explicit Managed boundary for a public runtime contract
scenarios.purpose: Check whether an explicit Planner entry handles a public runtime contract and compatibility decision before implementation.
scenarios.userInput: Use explicit `imm-planner` for this plan-only request in the copied Git fixture. The requested change would rename the packaged public runtime contract `plugins/immune-brain/runtime/v4_runtime.ts` and retain compatibility for existing consumers. Do not mutate runtime code or invent a compatibility layer. Resolve the source-repair and migration alternatives first; any necessary compatibility mechanism needs an owner, exit condition, and cleanup milestone. Keep candidate artifacts under docs/specs or docs/plans, author and stage a TaskIntent through the installed wrapper, and validate it without Enrollment.
successChecklist: The explicit `imm-planner` entry selects Managed planning; request wording alone is not treated as a route trigger.
The run creates only the bounded Managed planning artifact needed for later enrollment and does not implement before authority exists.
The response identifies compatibility and rollback verification instead of treating file count as the reason for Managed routing.

scenarios.title: Boundary on weak match
scenarios.purpose: Check whether the plugin narrows scope when the request should not trigger the full lifecycle workflow.
scenarios.userInput: This task is a weak match for Immune-Brain: design a marketing logo for the project. Do not create image assets or broaden into unrelated design work. In this fixture workspace only, read HANDOFF.md and README.md, then record a concise boundary note in HANDOFF.md explaining why the full Immune-Brain workflow is not appropriate and what minimal handoff, if any, remains. Do not run git commands. Do not inspect `plugins/immune-brain/skills`, `plugins/immune-brain/dist`, or create upstreams.
successChecklist: The run narrows scope instead of forcing a bad fit.
Any edit is limited to a boundary or handoff note.
